observations.body: Paul announces an allegory of two women and covenants, identifies Hagar with Mount Sinai and present Jerusalem in bondage, and contrasts her with the free woman and Jerusalem above.
observations.label: Paul allegorically associates Sinai with Hagar

observations.body: Paul allegorically associates Sinai with Hagar belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Galatians 4:21–31 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Galatians 4:21–31 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: Paul allegorically associates Sinai with Hagar belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
payload.title: Paul allegorically associates Sinai with Hagar
